title: On the Evaluation of Machine-Generated Reports
abstract: Presents an evaluation framework for long-form machine-generated reports intended to be complete, accurate, and verifiable. Completeness and accuracy are evaluated through information nuggets represented as questions and answers, while citations connect report claims to source documents for verifiability.

title: Auto-ARGUE: LLM-Based Report Generation Evaluation
abstract: Introduces an automated LLM-based implementation of the ARGUE framework for evaluating long-form citation-backed reports. Evaluation on the TREC 2024 NeuCLIR report-generation pilot shows good system-level correlation with human judgments and operationalizes report completeness, accuracy, and citation-oriented diagnostics.

title: Two-Level Meta-Rubrics for Evaluating Open-Ended Generation: GAMUT, a Benchmark for Factual Completeness
abstract: Targets the completeness side of long-form factuality rather than only precision of generated claims. A structured meta-rubric represents required content, importance, open-ended sets, processes, and relations, then compiles these requirements into binary checks scored by an LLM judge; the evidence-backed rubrics are verified by expert human annotators.

title: DEER: A Benchmark for Evaluating Deep Research Agents on Expert Report Generation
abstract: Evaluates evidence-based expert report generation with an expert-developed multidimensional rubric taxonomy and report-wide claim verification. Its verification architecture checks both cited and uncited claims, assesses evidence quality, and exposes logical-completeness failures that ordinary citation-presence measures can miss.

title: Selective Generation for Controllable Language Models
abstract: Develops selective-generation algorithms for language models that control a generation risk defined using textual entailment while retaining useful output. The method provides statistical control over false discoveries in generated sequences and studies supervised and semi-supervised settings.

title: Self-Evaluation Improves Selective Generation in Large Language Models
abstract: Studies selective generation for open-ended model outputs by reformulating self-evaluation into token-prediction tasks. It compares self-evaluation scoring strategies, including an explicit none-of-the-above option, and evaluates their ability to identify when generation should be withheld on TruthfulQA and TL;DR.

title: A Semantic-Sampling Framework for Evaluating Calibration in Open-Ended Question Answering
abstract: Introduces Sem-ECE for probability-calibration evaluation in genuinely open-ended QA. Answers are sampled and grouped into semantic classes whose frequencies provide confidence estimates, with same-sample and held-out estimators analyzed theoretically and evaluated on open-ended QA benchmarks.

title: Only Say What You Know: Calibration-Aware Generation for Long-Form Factuality
abstract: Proposes Calibration-Aware Generation, which separates exploratory reasoning from commitment to final claims. Intermediate information receives calibrated reliability estimates, allowing the model to prioritize reliable content and avoid committing uncertain material in long-form generation.

title: SAFER: Risk-Constrained Sample-then-Filter in Large Language Models
abstract: Introduces a two-stage risk-control method for open-ended QA. It calibrates a finite sampling budget and abstains when a requested risk level is infeasible, then conformalizes an uncertainty threshold for filtering unreliable candidates while controlling exclusion risk.

title: CAP: Conformalized Abstention Policies for Context-Adaptive Risk Management for LLMs and VLMs
abstract: Combines conformal prediction with reinforcement learning to learn context-dependent abstention policies rather than using one global risk level. The policy balances point prediction, prediction sets, and full abstention according to downstream utility and extends risk management to foundation-model outputs.
venue: Asian Conference on Machine Learning 2025, PMLR 304

title: QA-Calibration of Language Model Confidence Scores
abstract: Generalizes average calibration for generative QA to calibration across question-and-answer groups and develops post-hoc calibration procedures. The work is aimed at confidence estimates that are more meaningful for downstream decision-making than aggregate calibration alone.

title: Just Ask for Calibration: Strategies for Eliciting Calibrated Confidence Scores from Language Models Fine-Tuned with Human Feedback
abstract: Evaluates methods for obtaining calibrated answer confidence from RLHF-tuned language models. It finds that verbalized confidence can be better calibrated than conditional probabilities on several QA benchmarks and frames low confidence as a signal for deferral.

title: Teaching Models to Express Their Uncertainty in Words
abstract: Shows that a language model can generate verbalized probabilities whose reported confidence is empirically calibrated. It also tests calibration under distribution shift and introduces CalibratedMath for evaluating verbalized uncertainty.

title: Reducing Conversational Agents’ Overconfidence Through Linguistic Calibration
abstract: Studies whether free-form dialogue agents express verbal confidence or doubt in proportion to their factual correctness. It shows substantial miscalibration in existing agents and improves linguistic calibration by incorporating predicted correctness into controllable generation.
venue: Transactions of the Association for Computational Linguistics

title: Linguistic Calibration of Long-Form Generations
abstract: Defines linguistic calibration for long-form generation in terms of whether generated confidence statements enable calibrated downstream probabilistic judgments. A supervised-plus-reinforcement-learning approach produces long-form answers with calibrated uncertainty expressions, with automated and human evaluation and tests under substantial domain shift.

title: Atomic Calibration of LLMs in Long-Form Generations
abstract: Introduces atomic calibration for long-form text by decomposing responses into factual claims and evaluating confidence at that finer granularity. It compares discriminative and generative confidence elicitation and studies fusion strategies, addressing the failure of a single response-level confidence to represent mixed-correctness long-form outputs.

title: LoVeC: Reinforcement Learning for Better Verbalized Confidence in Long-Form Generation
abstract: Trains language models with reinforcement learning to append numerical confidence estimates to individual statements during long-form generation. Evaluation on long-form QA examines free-form and iterative confidence tagging and reports improved calibration and cross-domain generalization.

title: Think Through Uncertainty: Improving Long-Form Generation Factuality via Reasoning Calibration
abstract: Introduces a claim-aware reasoning protocol in which long-form outputs are decomposed into atomic claims carrying explicit confidence estimates. A multi-stage training pipeline aligns confidence with claim correctness, and the resulting confidence is used for selective abstention from uncertain claims.

title: Train for Truth, Keep the Skills: Binary Retrieval-Augmented Reward Mitigates Hallucinations
abstract: Uses an online reinforcement-learning reward based on whether generated output is fully consistent with retrieved evidence. Besides reducing long-form factual errors, the trained models develop selective abstention on short-form QA when their knowledge is insufficient while preserving performance on accepted answers.

title: Claim-Level Confidence Calibration for Reliable Decision Making with Large Language Models
abstract: Studies calibrated confidence for individual factual claims rather than whole responses. It combines atomic claim decomposition, consistency and self-verification signals, and post-hoc calibration, enabling low-confidence claims to be selectively sent for retrieval or human review.

title: Improving reliability of large language models via claim-level self-verification and uncertainty calibration
abstract: Presents CLAIM-CAL, which decomposes generated answers into atomic factual claims, applies multiple self-verification probes, aggregates them into an answer-level risk signal, and calibrates that signal post hoc. It evaluates calibrated confidence together with selective accuracy and coverage rather than relying only on error ranking.

title: SURE-RAG: Sufficiency and Uncertainty-Aware Evidence Verification for Selective Retrieval-Augmented Generation
abstract: Treats evidence sufficiency as a set-level property in selective RAG rather than equating passage relevance with adequate support. Its verifier aggregates evidence coverage, support strength, conflict, and uncertainty and permits answering only when the retrieved evidence set is judged sufficient.

title: MSRS: Evaluating Multi-Source Retrieval-Augmented Generation
abstract: Introduces benchmarks for retrieval and long-form synthesis when required information is distributed across multiple sources and no individual source is sufficient. The evaluation separates retrieval effectiveness from the ability to integrate and synthesize evidence across sources, including an oracle-retrieval setting.

title: A Closer Look at Claim Decomposition
abstract: Examines how claim-decomposition choices affect evaluation of whether generated text is supported by external knowledge. It introduces DecompScore and a decomposition method motivated by logical atomism, highlighting that compound text must be separated appropriately before support can be measured reliably.

title: Minimal Evidence Group Identification for Claim Verification
abstract: Formalizes the identification of minimal groups of evidence pieces that collectively provide full support for a claim. The formulation explicitly distinguishes full from partial support and allows multiple alternative evidence groups, making it relevant to evidence-completeness evaluation for multi-source claims.

title: Can LLMs Evaluate Complex Attribution in QA? Automatic Benchmarking using Knowledge Graphs
abstract: Introduces CAQA for evaluating complex evidence attribution with fine-grained attribution categories and deliberately subtle attribution differences. It benchmarks 25 automatic evaluators, compares them with human evaluators, and studies evaluators fine-tuned on the benchmark.

title: Decision-Focused Summarization
abstract: Defines summarization around the information needed for a downstream decision rather than generic textual salience. Its evaluation measures decision faithfulness and representativeness and includes a human study testing whether summaries preserve information needed to make the target decision.

title: Improving Meeting Summarization by Focusing on User Needs: A Task-Oriented Evaluation
abstract: Evaluates decision-focused meeting summaries by how well they support a concrete decision-debriefing task rather than by generic similarity alone. The study compares focused and general-purpose summaries using task effectiveness, report quality, efficiency, and user-perceived success.
venue: International Conference on Intelligent User Interfaces 2009

title: Evaluating Content Selection in Summarization: The Pyramid Method
abstract: Introduces the Pyramid Method for evaluating summary content selection using human-identified content units weighted by how often they appear across reference summaries. It provides a foundational mechanism for measuring coverage of important information, although it does not itself solve source attribution, temporal validity, or open-world completeness.

title: Agreement is overrated: A plea for correlation to assess human evaluation reliability
abstract: Examines reliability assessment in human evaluation of natural-language generation and argues that inter-annotator agreement alone is inadequate in the presence of legitimate linguistic variability. It recommends considering correlation together with agreement and supports the argument through a survey and case studies.

title: Systematic Evaluation of LLM-as-a-Judge in LLM Alignment Tasks: Explainable Metrics and Diverse Prompt Templates
abstract: Develops metrics for validating LLM judges while explicitly accounting for judge inconsistency and prompt-template sensitivity. Experiments compare judge outputs against human evaluators on alignment datasets and show that judge reliability varies materially with evaluation design.

title: Validating LLM-as-a-Judge Systems under Rating Indeterminacy
abstract: Shows that validation of LLM judges can be biased when human rating tasks admit several reasonable labels but evaluation collapses them to a single forced-choice gold rating. It develops a validation framework using response-set ratings and evaluates the approach across multiple real-world rating tasks and commercial models.

title: Program-Verifiable Evaluation for Temporal QA: Metrics for Evidence Validity
abstract: Separates answer correctness from the temporal validity of cited evidence in time-sensitive QA. It introduces program-verifiable metrics for evidence freshness and an oracle-answer diagnostic that can expose temporally invalid evidence even when the final answer is held correct.

title: Adaptive Conformal Inference Under Distribution Shift
abstract: Develops adaptive conformal inference for sequential data whose distribution changes over time in unknown ways. Instead of assuming exchangeability, the method adapts the conformal miscoverage level online and targets long-run coverage under distribution shift.

title: Conformal Risk Control
abstract: Generalizes conformal methods from prediction-set coverage to control of expected monotone loss functions. The framework supports finite-sample risk guarantees and includes applications relevant to structured outputs and question answering, with extensions for some forms of distribution shift.

title: Automatically Adaptive Conformal Risk Control
abstract: Develops conformal risk control that automatically adapts to input-dependent difficulty rather than relying solely on a single marginal risk target. The method provides approximate conditional risk control and is relevant to continuously adjusting acceptance policies under heterogeneous or changing inputs.

title: When Can Conformal Risk Control Certify LLM Outputs? Bounds, Impossibility, and Adaptation for Structured Generation
abstract: Studies when conformal risk control can certify structured language-model outputs and derives limits showing when a target risk requires abstention because base risk is too high. It also examines adaptation under cross-dataset shift, connecting statistical risk guarantees to selective generation.

title: SelectiveNet: A Deep Neural Network with an Integrated Reject Option
abstract: Introduces an end-to-end architecture that jointly learns prediction and rejection rather than thresholding a separately trained predictor. Evaluation centers on the risk-coverage trade-off, providing a foundational selective-prediction formulation transferable to generation.

title: Selective Classification for Deep Neural Networks
abstract: Develops selective classification methods that abstain on part of the input domain in order to meet a desired risk target with high probability. The paper provides an early modern formulation of empirical risk-coverage guarantees for deep predictors.

title: Optimal strategies for reject option classifiers
abstract: Unifies cost-based, bounded-risk, and bounded-coverage formulations of classification with a reject option. It characterizes their optimal prediction strategy and defines proper uncertainty scores sufficient for constructing selective prediction rules.

title: On Optimum Recognition Error and Reject Tradeoff
abstract: Provides a foundational decision-theoretic analysis of the trade-off between recognition error and rejection. It derives optimal reject rules as a function of the cost assigned to erroneous decisions and abstention.

title: Verification of Forecasts Expressed in Terms of Probability
abstract: Foundational work on verification of probabilistic forecasts that introduced the scoring formulation now known as the Brier score. It supplies a basic proper probabilistic evaluation tool for assessing whether confidence forecasts correspond to observed outcomes.

title: A Coefficient of Agreement for Nominal Scales
abstract: Introduces Cohen's kappa for measuring agreement between nominal-scale raters while accounting for agreement expected by chance. It is a foundational reliability statistic for human annotation, although agreement alone does not establish evaluator validity.

title: Selective prediction-set models with coverage guarantees
abstract: Develops models that either output prediction sets or abstain when uncertainty is high and supplies procedures for estimating and bounding selective coverage. Experiments include out-of-sample population shifts and recalibration of prediction-set coverage.
